ana: Heads up — our quantized bringup for hf/november-qa-1 is failing the regression suite. Many prompts truncate or end with extra <|pad|> tokens, and generated answers are cut off. I see a strange logits spike for token id 50257.
michael: Oof. Can you paste `tokenizer.get_vocab()` and the model's `added_tokens.json` from the HF repo? Also the redwood conversion command you used.
ana: Pasted below. Note: converter was `redwood convert --from hf --model-path ./hf-model --out ./rw-model --tokenizer ./hf-model/tokenizer` (default flags).
ana: `added_tokens.json` (from HF):
```json
{
  "added_tokens": [
    {"str": "<|bos|>", "id": 50256},
    {"str": "<|eos|>", "id": 50257},
    {"str": "<|pad|>", "id": 50258}
  ]
}
```
ana: `tokenizer.get_vocab()` (snippet):
```
{"the": 220, "to": 284, "<|eos|>": 50256, "<|unk|>": 0, "<|bos|>": 50257}
```
michael: Wait that's the mismatch — `added_tokens.json` says eos=50257 but the tokenizer vocab has eos=50256 and bos=50257. So IDs drifted relative to the file.
sriram: This smells like fast vs slow tokenizers assigning ids differently. The HF `added_tokens.json` isn't always authoritative for the final id allocation when you load a "fast" tokenizer; `tokenizers` may merge/vocab-order new tokens differently. When the redwood converter blindly reads added_tokens.json and reassigns ids, we can end up with double-mapped ids.
jen: I reproduced locally. Steps:
1) `tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('./hf-model', use_fast=True)`
2) `tokenizer.get_vocab()` shows bos/eos swapped vs the repo file.
3) `tokenizer.added_tokens_encoder` shows mapping used at runtime.
jen: Quick hack: `AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(..., use_fast=False)` yields the same ids as `added_tokens.json` in the repo for this model. So fast tokenizer ordering is the culprit for this repo.
ana: That explains why the quantized run (which loads the RW-converted token ids into the embedding table) was indexing the wrong rows — pad/eos mapped to the wrong embeddings and the LM terminated early.
michael: We should update the converter to always query `tokenizer.get_vocab()` (or `added_tokens_encoder`) after loading the tokenizer and persist the runtime ids into the RW metadata instead of trusting the repo json. Also add a check that `all(tokenizer.encode(special) == [expected_id])` for the special tokens.
sriram: Agreed. For now a quick workaround in bringup: in our conversion step run a small script that compares `repo_added = json.load(open('added_tokens.json'))` to `rt_vocab = tokenizer.get_vocab()` and emits a warning + mapping patch if ids differ.
ana: I ran a regression where I patched the RW model's token id map to match `tokenizer.get_vocab()` and reran the eval: perplexity dropped from 18.9 -> 12.6 and chat prompts stop truncating.
eval-bot: Regression check (hf/november-qa-1, quant-int8): before-patch PPL=18.9, after-patch PPL=12.6, samples failing length check 42 -> 3. Full report: https://ci.internal/reports/17688
jen: I'll open a PR against the converter: change behavior to prefer runtime tokenizer ids, add a CI job that loads models with both `use_fast=True/False` and asserts special token parity. Also add an integration test that runs a tiny decode and checks `all_special_tokens` mapping.
infra-bot: PR #2245 opened by jen: https://git.internal/rw/convert/pulls/2245 — running unit tests.
michael: Nice. After PR merges we should re-run the full quantized bringup and the deduped eval suite. Also add a note in the onboarding checklist: "Verify special token ids from runtime tokenizer (get_vocab()) before conversion".
ana: Thanks team — leaving a short reproducer in the model's README and will follow up if anything else pops up. :thumbsup:
